text:
Ava: FYI I ran a bring-up for rk-3b-ptq on the canonical holdout and the numbers are the usual mixed bag: NDCG@10 +0.017, MRR@10 -0.034.
Jon: Same pattern we've seen. Any upstream changes to candidate generation or sampling?
Ava: No deliberate changes, but I noticed the holdout sample for this run included ~3.5% more short queries (<=5 tokens) than baseline. That could amplify top1 sensitivity.
Priya: Do we have per-query compare artifacts? I find the fastest triage is diffing top1 across runs.
Ava: Yep. Ran: 
```
rerank.eval --run baseline --run ptq --compare-per-query --out per_query_diffs.json
```
Ava: Top1 flip rate = 5.4% on full holdout. Top3 flip rate = 2.1%.
Rex: 5.4% is too high. For quant models we expect some compression but not that much. Did you check candidate normalization parity? Small serializer diffs (html unescape, nbsp) can change tokenization and lexical tie-breakers.
Ava: Good call. I ran serializer_parity and found 1.9% candidate text diffs (mostly trailing spaces and & vs &).
Priya: That explains some flips. Action: unify serializer for eval and prod, but in parallel we should try a non-invasive mitigation: stable tiebreaker when score difference < 1e-3. That tends to reduce top1 churn.
Jon: Also try anchor_weight rescale. Quant tends to compress scores; anchor term might need a multiplicative adjustment (~0.95). Small sweep on a 20k sample is quick.
Ava: Did both. Anchor sweep [0.9,0.95,1.0]: MRR delta (vs baseline) on sample = [-0.012, -0.006, -0.034]. 0.95 looks promising.
Rex: Nice. What's the effect of stable tiebreaker?
Ava: Enabling stable doc_id tiebreak for abs(delta) < 1e-3 reduced top1 flip to 1.6% on the 20k sample and MRR delta improved to -0.007.
Priya: That suggests most of the MRR drop is from micro-noise flips. Two parallel steps: 1) land serializer parity PR in candidate pipeline 2) add quant model config to use anchor_weight=0.95 + stable-tiebreak. Keep the change in serving as config, not hardcode.
Jon: Also add onboarding CI gates: run a 10k fast-sample check where top1_flip_rate < 2% and MRR delta > -0.01 vs baseline, else block. File a review ticket if it fails.
Ava: Will do. I opened PRs: #ml-serializer-parity and #rk-quant-config. Tests: small sample runs attached.
eval-bot: run://2026-03-25/rk3b-ptq-sample completed. metrics: NDCG@10 0.749 -> 0.766, MRR@10 0.502 -> 0.468 (delta ndcg +0.017, delta mrr -0.034). artifacts: s3://eval/artifacts/runs/1766004321/
Ava: After applying anchor_weight=0.95 + stable tiebreak on the full holdout: rerun queued.
Ava: Also noting calibration seed variance: I re-calibrated PTQ with seed=7 vs seed=42 and saw tiny differences in top1 flip patterns but same aggregate MRR delta. So seed alone isn't the root cause.
Priya: Good to know. That points back to input parity + scoring scale. Please include cohort breakdown by query length and by "has_anchor" in the console output for the full run so we can quickly see where regressions concentrate.
Ava: Adding that. Quick interim: small-run with adjusted config shows MRR delta -0.009 and top1 flips 1.9% on 20k sample. Full holdout running now.
Jon: If full holdout confirms, we should ship the config mapping for quant variants: a simple model_metadata key that the serving stack reads to adjust anchor weight and tiebreak behavior. That way we don't change core scoring code.
Rex: Agree. Also add a lightweight parity check in model onboarding: serializer parity < 0.5% or fail. Saves a lot of time.
Ava: Will add both gates. Final note: when reporting to product, present both NDCG and MRR + cohort split and explain tie instability vs genuine quality change. Helps avoid false positives.
Ava: Full holdout finished: eval-bot posted artifacts. Final numbers: NDCG@10 0.749 -> 0.767 (+0.018), MRR@10 0.502 -> 0.496 (-0.006) with anchor_weight=0.95 + stable-tiebreak. Uploading diffs to PR comments.
Priya: Nice! That's acceptable delta. Please ship config mapping behind a feature flag and monitor online metrics for top1.
Jon: :thumbsup: great triage loop.
Rex: I'll file the small incident note about the serializer mismatch we found earlier so it's tracked.
Ava: thanks all, closing the loop in the PRs.
